    Dune Meadows III: Non-Euclidean Distance Diagnostics

    dune-distance-diagnostics.Rmd

    Bray–Curtis dissimilarity is often semimetric. The package uses its Gower-centred matrix directly and retains the entire eigenvalue spectrum.

    bray <- vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
bray_diagnostics <- distance_diagnostics(bray)

unlist(bray_diagnostics[c(
  "euclidean", "positive_inertia", "negative_inertia",
  "negative_count", "negative_ratio", "correction"
)])
#>            euclidean     positive_inertia     negative_inertia 
#>              "FALSE"   "4.59394689658881"  "0.294925026143221" 
#>       negative_count       negative_ratio           correction 
#>                  "5" "0.0641986145643552"               "none"

    Negative inertia is diagnostic information, not an error and not something the engine silently removes. The most negative eigenvalues are directly available.

    head(sort(bray_diagnostics$eigenvalues), 6)
#> [1] -9.678567e-02 -7.412306e-02 -5.473417e-02 -4.285699e-02 -2.642513e-02
#> [6] -2.894644e-17

    A square-root transformation is a separate sensitivity analysis. It changes the dissimilarity and therefore defines a different analysis.

    sqrt_bray <- sqrt(bray)
sqrt_diagnostics <- distance_diagnostics(sqrt_bray)

rbind(
  Bray_Curtis = c(
    negative_count = bray_diagnostics$negative_count,
    negative_ratio = bray_diagnostics$negative_ratio
  ),
  square_root_Bray = c(
    negative_count = sqrt_diagnostics$negative_count,
    negative_ratio = sqrt_diagnostics$negative_ratio
  )
)
#>                  negative_count negative_ratio
#> Bray_Curtis                   5     0.06419861
#> square_root_Bray              0     0.00000000

    The model results can likewise be compared, with identical permutation seeds.

    raw_fit <- permanova_oneway(
  bray, dune.env$Management,
  permutations = 199, seed = 20260718, engine = "projection"
)
sqrt_fit <- permanova_oneway(
  sqrt_bray, dune.env$Management,
  permutations = 199, seed = 20260718, engine = "projection"
)

rbind(
  Bray_Curtis = raw_fit$table[1, c("pseudo_f", "p_perm")],
  square_root_Bray = sqrt_fit$table[1, c("pseudo_f", "p_perm")]
)
#>                  pseudo_f p_perm
#> Bray_Curtis      2.767243  0.005
#> square_root_Bray 1.979245  0.005

    Lingoes or Cailliez corrections, when used elsewhere, should be reported with the same prominence: they are model sensitivities, never invisible cleanup.
